body: Social Security Act 2018 section 16: A person meets the residential requirement if the person is a New Zealand citizen or holds a residence class visa, is ordinarily resident in New Zealand when first applying, and has resided continuously in New Zealand for at least 2 years at any one time after becoming a citizen or resident, or is recognised as a refugee or protected person. A person also meets it if ordinarily resident in a country with a New Zealand reciprocity agreement and has resided continuously in New Zealand for at least 2 years before applying or before a decision is made. Regulations may specify circumstances in which a person is taken to meet the requirement or must not be required to comply.

Social Security Act 2018 section 18: A person is not entitled to receive at the same time, in the person's own right, more than 1 main benefit, or both a main benefit and New Zealand superannuation, or both a main benefit and a veteran's pension.

Social Security Act 2018 section 19: A person is not entitled or eligible to receive a benefit if the person is unlawfully resident or present in New Zealand, or is lawfully resident or present in New Zealand only by virtue of holding a temporary entry class visa. The section is subject to section 205.

Social Security Act 2018 section 20: A person is entitled to jobseeker support if the person has a work gap, is available for work, meets the age requirement, meets the residential requirement, and has no or minimum income.

Social Security Act 2018 section 21: A person has a work gap if not in full-time employment, or is in employment but losing earnings through a health condition or injury, including not working at all or working reduced hours. The person may treat a substitute payment during the health condition or injury as a loss of earnings.

Social Security Act 2018 section 22: A person is available for work if available for and seeking full-time employment, willing and able to undertake it, and has taken reasonable steps to find it; or would satisfy that test but for circumstances that would qualify the person for a work-test exemption; or is willing and able to undertake full-time employment but, because of health condition, injury, or disability, is limited in capacity to seek, undertake, or be available for it.
Social Security Act 2018 section 23: A jobseeker support applicant meets the age requirement if at least 18 years old without a dependent child, and at least 20 years old in any other case.

Social Security Act 2018 section 24: A person has no or minimum income if the person has no income or income of less than the amount that would reduce the applicable rate of jobseeker support to zero. If, during a temporary period, the person has enough income to reduce the applicable rate to zero but otherwise meets the requirements, entitlement is not affected by that income.

Social Security Act 2018 section 25: MSD may grant jobseeker support on hardship grounds to a person who is in hardship, is not entitled or eligible for any other main benefit, New Zealand superannuation, or veteran's pension, and cannot earn enough income to support the person and spouse, partner, or dependent children. It includes eligibility routes for people meeting specified section 20 requirements and for certain full-time students between academic years, including 16 or 17 year olds with a parental support gap or in a relationship.

Social Security Act 2018 section 26: A person is not entitled to, or eligible to be granted, jobseeker support if a full-time student unless eligible under section 25, unemployed because of the person's or same-workplace union members' participation in a strike, or MSD reasonably believes the person became unemployed or took leave with or without pay to undertake employment-related training.

Social Security Act 2018 section 29: A person is entitled to sole parent support if the person meets the sole parent requirement, is not in split care or is the 1 parent entitled in a split-care situation, meets the residential requirement, and is aged 20 years or over.

Social Security Act 2018 section 30: A person meets the sole parent requirement if the person is the mother or father of, and caring for, at least 1 dependent child aged under 14 years and is single, widowed, has a dissolved marriage or civil union, is living apart from and has lost support or is inadequately maintained by a spouse or partner, or has lost regular support because the spouse or partner is subject to imprisonment, supervision, intensive supervision, or home detention conditions preventing employment.

Social Security Act 2018 section 31: MSD may regard a dependent child as the applicant's child if the child is maintained by the applicant and was maintained by the applicant's spouse or partner, or if neither orphan's benefit nor unsupported child's benefit is payable and specified parental conditions are met, or if the child's parents are unwilling to support the child because of exceptional circumstances.

Social Security Act 2018 section 32: In a split-care situation, where parents live apart, each is principal caregiver of 1 or more of 2 or more dependent children, and both would otherwise be entitled to sole parent support, only 1 parent is entitled. The entitled parent is the one already receiving sole parent support for any child, otherwise the one MSD considers was principal caregiver before separation, otherwise the principal caregiver of the youngest child. The section does not apply if each parent became principal caregiver under court orders about day-to-day care.

Social Security Act 2018 section 33: Sole parent support expires and is replaced with jobseeker support on the date the youngest dependent child in the person's care turns 14, unless MSD reasonably believes the person would not meet jobseeker entitlement conditions, in which case sole parent support expires and MSD invites a jobseeker application.

Social Security Act 2018 section 34: A person is entitled to the supported living payment if the person has restricted work capacity or is totally blind, meets the residential requirement, and is aged 16 years or over.

Social Security Act 2018 section 35: A person has restricted work capacity if permanently and severely restricted in capacity for work because of a health condition, injury, or disability arising from an accident or existing from birth. Permanently restricted means MSD is satisfied that the condition is expected to continue for the required period in regulations, or the person is not expected to live for that period because terminal. Severely restricted means MSD is satisfied that the person is incapable of regularly working at least 15 hours a week in open employment.

Social Security Act 2018 section 36: A person must not be granted a supported living payment if MSD is satisfied that the restricted capacity for work or total blindness was self-inflicted and brought about with a view to qualifying for a benefit.

Social Security Act 2018 section 39: A person receiving supported living payment for permanent and severe restriction of work capacity who, with MSD's agreement, undertakes open employment for an agreed period does not lose entitlement by reason only of working 15 or more hours a week during the agreed period. The agreed open-employment period must not exceed 26 weeks.

Social Security Act 2018 section 40: A person is entitled to supported living payment as a carer if MSD is satisfied the person is required to give full-time care and attention at home to a person who would otherwise have to receive institutional care and who is not the carer's spouse or partner, the carer meets the residential requirement, and the carer is aged at least 18 without a dependent child or at least 20 in any other case. MSD may continue a payment for not more than 28 days even though the person cared for was not during that period in the carer's full-time care. Institutional care includes hospital, rest home, residential disability, or equivalent Oranga Tamariki care.
